tests.note: Loopback only (::1). The Sigma rule excludes 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 but not ::1, so an IPv6 loopback connection still exercises it; nothing leaves the machine.

inline.command: mkdir -p /tmp/zaafvesper && printf 'public class Z { public static void main(String[] a) throws Exception { new ProcessBuilder("/bin/sh","-c","id").inheritIO().start().waitFor(); Thread.sleep(3000); } }\n' > /tmp/zaafvesper/Z.java && java /tmp/zaafvesper/Z.java

tests.note: Needs a JDK on the runner image (single-file source launch). The JVM stays up 3 s after its child, as a server would: Sysmon for Linux reports the forking thread as the parent, and the sensor maps it to the JVM through /proc only while that thread exists.

bash copied under the name nginx starts whoami a second after it starts, as a running web server with a webshell would. (Without the pause, Sysmon for Linux can report the child before the parent's exec, so the parent still looks like bash.)
